concept.name: Steepener
concept.definition: A yield curve spread trade that gains when the yield differential between longer-maturity and shorter-maturity rates increases (the curve steepens). It is executed long the front (shorter-maturity) leg and short the back (longer-maturity) leg, typically with Treasury futures or cash bonds weighted to be DV01-neutral.
concept.intuition: You are betting the gap between long-term and short-term interest rates widens — whatever happens to the overall level of rates.
concept.mechanics: Buy the spread: long the short-end instrument (e.g. 2-year Treasury futures) and short the long-end instrument (e.g. 10- or 30-year futures). Because the back leg has a larger DV01, a hedge ratio is computed so the position is DV01-neutral and P&L depends on the spread change rather than parallel rate moves; CME Group lists fixed-ratio yield curve spreads (e.g. NOB, TUF) for simplified execution.
concept.formula: Curve spread = y_long_maturity - y_short_maturity; steepener P&L approx = (change in spread in bp) * position DV01.
concept.failure_modes: DV01-neutral construction still carries curve-shape (butterfly) and convexity risk, and the hedge ratio drifts as yields move, requiring rebalancing. Fixed-ratio exchange spreads simplify execution but leave residual ('tail') DV01 risk. Steepening driven by a violent bear move can inflict mark-to-market pain through margin even when the spread view is right.
concept.misconceptions: A steepener is not a bet that rates will rise or fall — it isolates the slope. 'Buy the spread' in steepener context means long front leg/short back leg, which is the opposite of buying the longer-maturity yield; quoting conventions ('net change') confuse newcomers.
concept.example: A trader buys 2-year Treasury futures and sells 10-year futures DV01-neutral when the 2s10s spread is -30 bp; if the spread widens to +20 bp, the position profits by roughly 50 bp times the position DV01.

citations.source: CME Group: Yield Curve Spread Trades - Opportunities & Applications
